title: Emergent Model Ecosystem Whitespace Assessment & Response Playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: Rapidly identify niche or emergent model capabilities (micro-vertical and specialty flavors) that create operational or product opportunities for Redwood Inference. Deliver a reproducible playbook that the PM and Scout teams can run every 2 weeks to surface high-value model entrants, quantify their deployment fit (latency/cost/compatibility), and recommend product responses (cataloging, quantized fallback recipes, dedicated capacity offers).
background: Recent field reports and partner telemetry suggest multiple small-model entrants optimized for narrow domains (legal reasoning, clinical summarization, internal knowledge RAG for fintech) are gaining traction in pilot customers. These entrants are often lower-cost and sometimes incompatible with our current runtime optimizations or quantization paths. We need a structured way to detect these threats/opportunities before they materially impact procurement choices.
scope:
- Scouting: automated signal sources + manual review (GitHub, Hugging Face, paperswithcode, vendor newsletters, Slack/sales reports).
- Triaging: rapid compatibility matrix (API/weights/quant support/seq len), latency/cost delta estimation, risk to existing product bundles.
- Field probes: 3 synthetic workloads per vertical to validate behavior and perf on comparable infra.
- Recommendations: keeper list (model variants to onboard as fallbacks), pricing/packaging hooks for Dedicated/Hosted, and guardrails for Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Automated scouting pipeline prototype that ingests 5 signal sources and normalizes candidate metadata
A 1-page compatibility matrix template and at least 8 completed triages across 4 verticals (legal, healthcare, fintech, e-commerce)
Synthetic workload test harness with perf & quality metrics (latency p50/p95, tokens/s, simple ROUGE/EM proxies) runnable in CI
Playbook doc with step-by-step triage run, triage scoring rubric, and three recommended go/no-go actions per candidate
Stakeholder sign-off from Runtime, Sales Ops, and Security on the triage rubric and sample outputs
tasks: Define signal sources and weighting (owner: Marcus)
Build minimal ingestion pipeline (owner: Eng - Scout team)
Design triage template and rubric (owner: PM)
Identify 12 candidate models from signals (owner: PM + Research)
Run synthetic workloads on Dedicated-like infra (owner: Eng - Performance)
Score each candidate and draft recommended response (owner: PM)
Review findings with Runtime and Security (owner: PM)
Publish playbook and add automation to weekly scout chore (owner: PM)
dependencies: PM-314159 (access to Sales pilot signal feed)
risks: Signal noise: high false-positive rate requiring more manual triage
Perf mismatch: synthetic workload not representative of real customer RAG prompts
Licensing surprises: candidate models may have unexpected commercial restrictions
Security gaps: some model weights or tooling may not pass enterprise private-deploy controls
deliverables: Emergent Model Scouting Pipeline (minimal viable data output)
Triaged Candidate Tracker (sheet + matrix) with 12 entries
Synthetic workload harness and baseline results for each candidate
Playbook doc: reproducible steps, rubric, and recommended product actions
One pager for sales: Threats & Opportunities summary
timeline: Week 1: finalize sources, ingestion prototype, triage rubric
Week 2: populate candidates, run synthetic probes on sample infra
Week 3: score and draft recommendations, stakeholder reviews
Week 4: publish playbook, onboard weekly scout cadence
metrics_of_success: Median time from signal->triage reduced to <= 10 business days
At least 3 candidate models with clear, actionable product responses (onboard/fallback/pricing)
Reduction in surprise procurement events from field by 40% in next quarter
Playbook adopted by cross-functional scout team and run 2x/month
